composio.note: Composio provides a managed Todoist OAuth app; use your own client ID and secret in a custom auth config for branding or dedicated quota.

need_own_app.answer: Not to prototype: Composio's managed Todoist app works. For launch, bring your own app if users should see your app name on consent, or you want dedicated quota and shorter polling.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio
Dedicated API quota instead of quota shared across Composio users

prerequisites.title: Verified Todoist account
prerequisites.detail: Certification starts with a verified Todoist user account. Todoist will help if you need a Pro account for development.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URIs
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing) and configured in the App Management Console.

steps.title: Create app in App Management Console
steps.detail: Log in, create the application and add your redirect URI(s). Copy the Client ID and Secret.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and register it in the Todoist app.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and the redirect URI matches.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Pick the narrowest scopes, such as data:read or data:read_write, and avoid restricted scopes.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and demo video
steps.detail: Draft the description, install instructions and disclaimer; prepare a 250x250 JPG icon and 1600x1000 JPG screenshots.
steps.done_when: All form fields are ready in English.

steps.title: Record demo and submit certification
steps.detail: Record the demo video and submit the form.

steps.title: Wait for Todoist review
steps.detail: Respond to feedback; email replies usually take about two business days.

traps.title: Token limit can block your app
traps.detail: If the app exceeds the maximum token limit or is suspended for abuse, users are redirected with an invalid_application_status error. The limit value was not found.

traps.title: Multiple redirect URIs need redirect_uri
traps.detail: With several redirect URIs configured, omitting redirect_uri in the authorization request is rejected with invalid_request.

traps.title: Naming and disclaimer rules
traps.detail: Todoist cannot be the primary app name; use 'x for Todoist'. The description must say it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

traps.title: Passing criteria are not guaranteed
traps.detail: Meeting the listed criteria does not guarantee certification. Apps that only work via Zapier/IFTTT or replicate Todoist features are not accepted.

traps.title: Restricted scopes are rejected
traps.detail: Scopes that are unknown or restricted to first-party use return invalid_scope.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded the maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Todoist; the limit value is not documented in the dossier.

open_questions: What is the maximum token limit per app? Ask Todoist developer support or check the App Management Console.
What are the exact API request rate limits? The docs reference a Request Limits section without published values; check it directly.
Does Todoist require re-review of certified apps after changes? Not found; ask Todoist via the submission email.

evidence.answer: The dynamic client registration endpoint is rate limited per caller.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: You can use our API for free, but depending on your Todoist account plan (or that of the authenticated user), some
evidence.answer: The API can be used for free, but some features may be restricted depending on the Todoist plan of the developer or the authenticated user.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: To authenticate other users, your application will need to obtain a token from
evidence.answer: To authenticate other users, the developer's application must obtain a token from each of them through the OAuth protocol.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The webhook for a specific user is activated when that user completes the OAuth flow of the app that declares the webhook.
evidence.answer: A user's webhook is activated when that user completes the OAuth flow of the app that declares the webhook.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: To activate webhooks for personal use, you need to complete the OAuth process with your account.
evidence.answer: To activate webhooks for personal use, a user must complete the OAuth process with their own account.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If your application has multiple redirect URIs configured, this parameter is required — the request will be rejected with invalid_request if it is omitted.
evidence.answer: If an app has multiple redirect URIs configured, the redirect_uri parameter is required and the request is rejected with invalid_request if it is omitted.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
evidence.answer: A redirect URI must be configured in the App Management Console, or the request fails with a JSON error.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Array of redirect URIs. Up to 10 entries, each ≤512 characters. Must be HTTPS (localhost is allowed for testing).
evidence.answer: Dynamic client registration accepts up to 10 redirect URIs, each up to 512 characters, which must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Non-empty array of redirect URIs. Must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).
evidence.answer: For Client ID Metadata Documents, the redirect URIs array must be non-empty and use HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: A field failed validation — e.g. a redirect URI is malformed or not HTTPS, or grant_types omits authorization_code
evidence.answer: A redirect URI that is malformed or not HTTPS, or a grant_types value that omits authorization_code, fails client metadata validation.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The document URL failed SSRF validation (HTTP, private IP, missing path), the document is malformed, exceeds the size limit, or client_id inside the document does not match the URL:
evidence.answer: Client ID Metadata Document URLs are checked for SSRF; HTTP URLs, private IPs, or a missing path fail, and redirects are not followed when fetching the document.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Redirects are not followed.
evidence.answer: Redirects are not followed when fetching a Client ID Metadata Document.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: For security reasons, Todoist only allows webhook urls that have HTTPS enabled and no ports specified in the url.
evidence.answer: Webhook URLs must use HTTPS and must not specify a port.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Before getting started, developers need to create their applications
evidence.answer: Developers create their applications in the App Management Console and configure one or more valid OAuth2 redirect URLs.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: A registered Todoist application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret which are needed for the OAuth2 flow.
evidence.answer: A registered application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret, which are needed for the OAuth2 flow.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Integrations can be created and updated here
evidence.answer: Integrations can be created and updated on the Todoist integrations page linked from the docs.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: "Todoist" cannot be the primary name of your app.
evidence.answer: The app name cannot use Todoist as its primary name; a format such as 'x for Todoist' or 'x with Todoist' is expected.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: that signals independence, such as "x for Todoist" or "x with Todoist".
evidence.answer: Names should signal independence, such as 'x for Todoist' or 'x with Todoist'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application description must state that it is "not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist."
evidence.answer: The app description must state that it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: but you must keep it clearly distinct from Todoist's official
evidence.answer: Apps referencing Todoist must keep it clearly distinct from Todoist's official products.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any use of Todoist's marks must comply with our
evidence.answer: Any use of Todoist's marks must comply with Todoist's brand guidelines.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: By using Todoist branding you agree to follow our brand
evidence.answer: Using Todoist branding means agreeing to follow the brand guidelines and Terms of Service.
